meta.regime: Two regimes changed at once. (1) THE YEN IS NOW DEFENDED AND HAWKISH. Japan's MoF is judged to have intervened late Thursday, spiking the yen ~3.3% from the 40-year low of 164 to 157.97 before a partial retrace to ~160-161; hours later the BoJ held 1.00% but Hajime Takata dissented FOR a hike, the Outlook Report upgraded FY26 GDP to ~0.8%, and the Bank said core inflation will run clearly above 2% from the second half of FY26 - citing wage pass-through, higher crude and the weak yen itself. A defended currency with a hawkish central bank is not a funding currency: the whole XXX/JPY carry book from yesterday has to come off. (2) THE IRAN PAUSE FAILED. After the brief late-July halt, the IRGC fired ballistic missiles at US forces and Trump said Iran is going to get a beating; WTI is back near $86 and Brent ~$91. Hormuz traffic has partially recovered under US naval escort (14 commodity vessels Wednesday vs single digits the prior week, ~6.5 mb/d out of the gulf versus a normal ~20 mb/d) but the waterway is still badly impaired. Meanwhile the dollar stays soft: June PCE cooled to 3.7% headline and 3.3% core with core m/m only +0.1%, on top of Q2 GDP at 1.5% and June payrolls at +57k - though the market still prices roughly a 63% chance of a September hike. Net: soft dollar, firm oil, live havens (gold + franc), a defended yen, and a widening AUD-vs-NZD policy split.
meta.nextBigEvent: US July employment report (Fri Aug 7, 12:30Z). June printed +57k with unemployment at 4.2% and April-May revised down 74k combined; another sub-100k print would kill the September hike the three FOMC dissenters are pushing and break the dollar lower, while a rebound re-arms it. It is the single biggest gate before July CPI on Aug 12.

dailyRead: The yen trade inverted overnight and that is the story of the day. Japan's Ministry of Finance is judged to have intervened late Thursday, spiking the yen roughly 3.3% and taking USD/JPY from the 40-year low of 164 down to 157.97 - a two-month low - before it retraced to around 160-161. Then the Bank of Japan held at 1.00% but with Hajime Takata dissenting FOR a hike, upgraded FY26 GDP to about 0.8% in the Outlook Report, and said core inflation is likely to run clearly above 2% from the second half of FY26, explicitly blaming wage pass-through, the rise in crude and the yen's own depreciation. That combination - an actively defended currency plus a central bank whose own forecasts now argue for tightening - removes the yen from the funding-currency bucket. Every XXX/JPY carry long that worked yesterday (NZD/JPY, CAD/JPY, GBP/JPY, EUR/JPY) has to come off; USD/JPY flips from a short-tilt RANGE to an outright SHORT, JPYBASKET flips from RANGE to LONG, and the honest read on the crosses where both legs are firm is RANGE, not short. On the dollar, June PCE cooled: headline 3.7% from 4.1%, core 3.3% from 3.4%, and core only +0.1% m/m against +0.2% expected, with goods prices down 0.6% - the softest goods print since November 2023. That sits on top of Q2 GDP at 1.5% and June payrolls at +57k with unemployment at 4.2%, so the dollar stays soft even though the market still prices about a 63% chance of a September hike off the three hawkish FOMC dissents. Geopolitically the de-escalation hope from earlier in the week is dead: the IRGC fired ballistic missiles at US forces, Trump said Iran is going to get a beating, and WTI is back near $86 with Brent around $91. Hormuz traffic has partially recovered under US naval escort - 14 commodity vessels crossed Wednesday against single digits the previous week, roughly 6.5 million barrels a day leaving the gulf versus a normal ~20 - but the strait remains badly impaired and the premium is re-established, which restores conviction in USOIL LONG and in CAD's terms-of-trade bid. Cleanest expressions today: AUD/NZD SHORT is now the highest-conviction trade on the board - Australia's Q2 trimmed mean missed at 3.6% (versus 3.7% expected, down from 3.7%) and the market prices only a 4% chance of an August RBA hike, while the RBNZ has already hiked to 2.50% and signalled that as the first of roughly three moves toward a neutral 3% by February, with the 4.1% Q2 CPI and $86 crude keeping its petrol engine hot. Then USD/JPY SHORT and JPYBASKET LONG on the yen regime change; EUR/USD and GBP/USD LONG on the soft dollar (cable with the extra kicker of the BoE's hawkish 6-3 hold); USD/CAD and USD/CHF SHORT; XAU LONG near $4,086 after cresting $4,100 and XAG LONG above $58; and USOIL LONG with conviction restored to MED. The caveat that governs the whole book: MoF has intervened once and can do it again into any yen weakness, so yen-cross positions must be sized for a violent second strike, and a genuine Iran ceasefire would snap the oil and haven premium back in a session.

today.read: This is a regime change, not a headline: an actively defended currency whose central bank's own forecasts now argue for tightening is no longer a funding currency. Take the XXX/JPY carry book off - USD/JPY flips to SHORT, JPYBASKET flips to LONG, and the crosses where both legs are firm (EUR, GBP, NZD, CAD, CHF vs JPY) are RANGE, not shorts. Risk: MoF's record 11.7trn yen operation in April/May failed to hold within six weeks, so a dollar bounce can re-pin it higher.

catalysts.event: Iran/US - pause FAILED, strikes resumed; Strait of Hormuz still impaired
catalysts.note: The late-July halt collapsed: the IRGC fired ballistic missiles at US forces and Trump said Iran is going to get a beating. WTI ~$86, Brent ~$91. Hormuz traffic has partially recovered under US naval escort - 14 commodity vessels crossed Wednesday versus single digits the prior week, and roughly 6.5 mb/d left the gulf against a normal ~20 - but the waterway remains badly impaired. A genuine ceasefire OR a systemic escalation is the two-way swing factor over the whole book.

catalysts.event: MoF intervention watch - second strike risk after Thursday's operation
catalysts.note: The MoF is judged to have intervened late Thursday, taking USD/JPY from the 40-year low of 164 to 157.97 before a retrace to ~160-161. The record 11.7trn yen April/May operation failed to hold within six weeks, so authorities have both the willingness and the recent precedent to strike again on any move back toward 164. Size every yen-cross position for it.

The biggest gate on the calendar. June printed +57k with unemployment at 4.2% and April-May revised down 74k combined; another sub-100k print kills the September hike and breaks the dollar lower, while a rebound re-arms it.
The Q2 trimmed mean miss at 3.6% collapsed August hike odds to 4% - a pause-and-observe hold is the base case and is already priced.
The disinflation test after June PCE cooled to 3.7% headline and 3.3% core. Decides whether the three FOMC dissenters get their September hike or the soft-data camp wins.
Live for a back-to-back hike after the 4.1% Q2 print and the Bank's own signal that July's move was the first of roughly three toward a neutral 3% by February.
Roughly 63% priced for a hike off the three July dissents, but the July jobs and CPI prints stand between here and there.

geopolitics: The de-escalation trade is dead and the oil premium is re-established. After the brief late-July halt that knocked WTI to ~$84.83 and Brent below $90, Iran's Revolutionary Guard fired ballistic missiles at US forces and Trump told Fox News that Iran is going to get a beating; WTI is back near $86 and Brent around $91. The Strait of Hormuz is in a partial, escorted recovery rather than a reopening: fourteen commodity vessels crossed in both directions on Wednesday against single digits the prior week, Qatar shipped its first LNG cargo out in three weeks, and roughly 6.5 million barrels a day left the gulf over the past week - against a normal throughput closer to 20 million - with the US Navy escorting tankers and at least one carrier transiting with its transponder off. Iranian attacks on tankers continue and Houthi strikes on Saudi pipeline infrastructure to Yanbu have taken out part of the workaround route. FX transmission: (1) CAD's terms-of-trade bid is restored - USD/CAD SHORT with conviction back to MED, though CAD is domestically weak with core inflation at 1.8-1.9%, five-year lows. (2) CHF's haven bid is re-armed and the SNB has softened its pledge to lean against franc strength - USD/CHF SHORT. (3) Gold at ~$4,086 and silver above $58 stay bid on the combination of soft dollar, war premium and oil-led inflation expectations. (4) Critically, firm crude now cuts BOTH ways for the yen: it is an importer drag, but the BoJ explicitly cited the rise in crude oil prices as one reason core inflation will run clearly above 2% from H2 FY26 - so oil strength is now partly a yen-hawkish input, not just a yen-negative one, which is why the XXX/JPY carry longs come off rather than get sized up. (5) High-beta AUD is the currency this tape punishes hardest, while NZD is cushioned because $86 crude sustains the petrol-CPI engine behind its 4.1% Q2 print. (6) USOIL LONG conviction is raised to MED, but Hormuz traffic is already recovering under escort and a genuine ceasefire would snap the premium back in a session - keep it sized for two-way headlines.
